package_info.package_name: N/A (RepoJacking attack enables arbitrary malicious package creation)
package_info.package_manager: Go/Swift/PHP (any language that pulls code directly from GitHub repositories)
package_info.package_versions: All versions of packages whose GitHub repositories were hijacked via RepoJacking
package_info.why_malicious: The entire package is considered malicious because attackers can take over the original repository namespace and publish code under a trusted name, serving arbitrary malicious code to users and applications that depend on the original repository.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (when package is fetched from hijacked repository)
execution_context.file_location: main.go (or equivalent entrypoint in the hijacked repository)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code accesses the SECRET_TOKEN environment variable and sends its value to a hardcoded domain via HTTP POST, enabling credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code exfiltrates sensitive environment variables to an external server, which is a classic sign of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal open-source packages do not access environment variables and send them to external domains during import or build.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate telemetry or error reporting might send non-sensitive data, but never secrets or tokens.
key_indicators: Access to environment variables unrelated to package function
Hardcoded external domain for data exfiltration

execution_context.trigger: import-time (when package is fetched from hijacked repository)
execution_context.file_location: main.swift (or equivalent entrypoint in the hijacked repository)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code downloads a remote payload from a hardcoded domain and writes it to the local filesystem, enabling further compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code downloads and writes a remote file without user consent, which is a common malware delivery technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages do not fetch and execute remote code during import or build.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Auto-updaters may fetch code, but only with explicit user consent and from trusted sources.
key_indicators: Automatic download and write to filesystem

attack_chain.action: Attacker claims a previously retired GitHub namespace by creating a repository with the target name and then renaming their account.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker controls the trusted repository namespace.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uploads malicious code to the hijacked repository.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is now served to all users fetching the package.

attack_chain.action: Users or CI systems import or build the package, executing the malicious code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Credential exfiltration, remote payload delivery, or further compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected network requests during package import or build
Access to environment variables or sensitive files in package code
Automatic download and execution of remote payloads
file_indicators: Sudden changes in main.go, main.swift, or other entrypoint files in a previously trusted repository
Presence of hardcoded external URLs in code
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to domains not previously associated with the package
Connections to attacker-controlled domains (e.g., attacker.com/exfil, attacker.com/payload)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for changes in trusted repositories, especially after account renames. Flag packages that make network requests or access sensitive environment variables during import or build. Alert on hardcoded external domains in package code, and track unexpected outbound connections from build or CI environments to unknown domains.
